title: Promises, Async/Await & Resilient Error Pipelines
summary: Master Promise internals, state machines, async/await mechanics, error propagation, and combinators (all, allSettled, race, any).
learningObjectives: Select and implement optimal Promise combinators (allSettled, race, any) based on fault tolerance requirements
Build resilient asynchronous workflows incorporating AbortController cancellation tokens and retry policies

sections.heading: 1. The Promise State Machine & Async/Await Under the Hood
sections.content:
A Promise represents the eventual result of an asynchronous operation. Internally, a Promise operates as a strict state machine with three mutually exclusive states:
1. Pending: Initial state; neither fulfilled nor rejected.
2. Fulfilled: Operation completed successfully; holds a permanent value.
3. Rejected: Operation failed; holds a permanent reason (error).

State transitions are irreversible: once fulfilled or rejected, a Promise is 'settled' and can never change state or fire callbacks again.

Promise Combinators:
- `Promise.all([p1, p2])`: Fails fast! Rejects immediately if ANY promise rejects. Resolves only when all succeed.
- `Promise.allSettled([p1, p2])`: Resilient! Waits for all promises to settle and returns an array of `{status: 'fulfilled', value}` or `{status: 'rejected', reason}` objects. Ideal for batch jobs where partial success is acceptable.
- `Promise.race([p1, p2])`: Settles with the outcome of the FASTEST promise (whether success or error). Used for request timeouts.
- `Promise.any([p1, p2])`: Resolves with the first SUCCESSFUL promise. Rejects with an `AggregateError` only if all promises fail.

`async`/`await` is syntactic sugar built on top of Promises and Generators. An `async` function always returns a Promise; `await` pauses execution of the async function until the awaited promise settles, without blocking the main event loop.

codeExamples.code:
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| PROMISE STATE MACHINE & ASYNC/AWAIT SUSPENSION                    |
|                                                                   |
|                   +------------------+                            |
|                   |     PENDING      |                            |
|                   +------------------+                            |
|                      /            \                              |
|          resolve(v) /              \ reject(err)                  |
|                    v                v                             |
|          +-------------+      +-------------+                     |
|          |  FULFILLED  |      |  REJECTED   |                     |
|          +-------------+      +-------------+                     |
|                 |                    |                            |
|                 v                    v                            |
|           .then(onSuccess)     .catch(onError)                    |
|                                                                   |
|  await promise:                                                   |
|  Function frame suspended -> Event Loop continues other work      |
|  On settlement -> Microtask resumes function execution frame.     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
codeExamples.explanation: Promises transition from pending to fulfilled or rejected once. Await pauses function execution without blocking the event loop.

keyPoints: Promises are immutable once settled; state changes cannot be undone.
Use Promise.allSettled when individual failures should not cancel remaining independent requests.
Unhandled promise rejections crash Node.js processes; always attach .catch() or wrap in try/catch.
commonMistakes: Using sequential 'await' inside a loop when operations are independent, accidentally turning parallel work into a slow waterfall.
Creating naked Promises with 'new Promise' when existing APIs already return standard promises.

sections.heading: 2. Production-Grade Fetch with Timeout via AbortController
sections.content: In production networks, hanging HTTP requests tie up connection pools. Using `AbortController` allows clients to enforce strict timeout deadlines, freeing resources immediately if a remote service fails to respond.

codeExamples.explanation: Demonstrates defensive timeout management using AbortController and strict cleanup in finally blocks.

keyPoints: Always clear timer IDs in finally blocks to prevent memory leaks.
AbortController signals can be shared across multiple child promises for unified cancellation.
commonMistakes: Awaiting requests inside for-loops sequentially instead of firing concurrently with Promise.all() or Promise.allSettled().

exercises.title: Implement a Batch Task Runner with Partial Failure Resilience
exercises.objective: Build a batch job runner using Promise.allSettled that reports successful items and aggregates failures.
exercises.description: Create runBatch(tasks) where tasks is an array of functions returning promises. Execute them concurrently, aggregate outcomes using Promise.allSettled, and return `{ successful: [...], failed: [...] }` without throwing unhandled exceptions.
instructions: Execute all tasks concurrently using Promise.allSettled.
Iterate through results and classify fulfilled vs rejected outcomes.
hints: Map functions to promises: `const promises = taskFunctions.map(fn => fn());`.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Promise.allSettled prevents one failing task from terminating the batch, enabling partial success reporting.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: How does Promise.allSettled differ from Promise.all?

options.text: Promise.allSettled rejects if any promise fails; Promise.all waits for all.
Promise.allSettled always waits for every promise to finish regardless of success or failure; Promise.all rejects immediately upon the first failure.
Promise.allSettled runs tasks in sequential order; Promise.all runs in parallel.
Promise.allSettled can only be used in Node.js.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Promise.all fails fast on the first rejection, whereas Promise.allSettled waits for all promises to settle, capturing all results and errors.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What happens if an error is thrown inside an async function without a try/catch block?

options.text: The function returns a Promise in the rejected state containing the thrown error.
The function converts the error to null.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Any uncaught exception inside an async function automatically rejects the returned promise with the thrown exception.

recap: Promises model asynchronous state. Use Promise.allSettled for resilient batch operations, AbortController for deadline cancellation, and try/catch/finally for clean error propagation.
